lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: weekly meal planning for balance and budget

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic weekly meal planning for balance and budget task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner is given a weekly budget ceiling written on the task sheet and a short list of food group categories (grains, protein, vegetables, fruits, dairy) with example items and estimated per-serving prices.
safetyNotes: This task is a written planning exercise only; no food is prepared, and no money changes hands as part of the lesson.
materials: learner-local: the provided weekly budget ceiling and food-group price list
learner-local: a calculator or the ability to add decimals by hand

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Describe one specific tradeoff you made between a food you would have preferred and a lower-cost item you chose instead, and explain how you kept the day nutritionally balanced anyway.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Nutritional balance across the week: All seven days include at least one item from each of the five food groups. | Budget estimation and adjustment: The weekly total is calculated correctly using the provided prices and fits at or under the budget ceiling. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner replan the same week at a budget ceiling ten percent lower than the original, identifying which two specific items they would substitute first to absorb the cut without dropping a food group.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic weekly meal planning for balance and budget task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the provided weekly budget ceiling and food-group price list
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: a calculator or the ability to add decimals by hand
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: weekly meal planning for balance and budget worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner is given a weekly budget ceiling written on the task sheet and a short list of food group categories (grains, protein, vegetables, fruits, dairy) with example items and estimated per-serving prices.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact weekly meal planning for balance and budget decision or action.
Model move 2: Before planning, estimate how much a household typically spends on food in one week.

Model move 3: Using the provided food-group price list, fill in one full day of the meal plan grid (breakfast, lunch, dinner) so it includes at least one item from each of the five food groups, and add up its estimated cost.

Model check: Nutritional balance across the week: All seven days include at least one item from each of the five food groups. | Budget estimation and adjustment: The weekly total is calculated correctly using the provided prices and fits at or under the budget ceiling.

resources.title: weekly meal planning for balance and budget action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for weekly meal planning for balance and budget.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: weekly meal planning for balance and budget coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner is given a weekly budget ceiling written on the task sheet and a short list of food group categories (grains, protein, vegetables, fruits, dairy) with example items and estimated per-serving prices.
Coach direction: Before planning, estimate how much a household typically spends on food in one week.
Learner prompt: Write your estimate for a one-week food total for a household, and list one specific reason your number might be too high or too low.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: weekly meal planning for balance and budget complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Using the provided food-group price list, fill in one full day of the meal plan grid (breakfast, lunch, dinner) so it includes at least one item from each of the five food groups, and add up its estimated cost.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My sample day includes at least one grain, one protein, one vegetable, one fruit, and one dairy item.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Show your addition for the sample day's estimated total cost using the provided per-serving prices.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: weekly meal planning for balance and budget minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe one specific tradeoff you made between a food you would have preferred and a lower-cost item you chose instead, and explain how you kept the day nutritionally balanced anyway.

Success checks: Nutritional balance across the week: All seven days include at least one item from each of the five food groups. | Budget estimation and adjustment: The weekly total is calculated correctly using the provided prices and fits at or under the budget ceiling.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: weekly meal planning for balance and budget supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional weekly meal planning for balance and budget condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Nutritional balance across the week: All seven days include at least one item from each of the five food groups. | Budget estimation and adjustment: The weekly total is calculated correctly using the provided prices and fits at or under the budget ceiling..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: weekly meal planning for balance and budget — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
